question: What are vital statistics primarily records of?

options.A: Life events in a human population

explanation: Vital statistics focus strictly on tracking core life events such as births, deaths, and marriages within a community. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why do community health nurses need to understand vital statistics?

options.A: To diagnose rare diseases in individual patients
options.B: To calculate daily hospital meal portions
options.C: To see the health trends of the entire community
options.D: To manage the financial payroll of the ward

explanation: Looking at population numbers helps nurses understand broader health patterns rather than just focusing on one sick person at a time. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary legal method for continuously recording births and deaths?
explanation: Civil registration is the official, continuous government process of recording vital events as they happen in real-time. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h2)

question: When would a community health team rely on a sample survey instead of a census?

options.B: When complete registration is not possible
options.C: When every single citizen comes to the clinic
options.D: When the government wants to count every building

explanation: Sample surveys are used to gather reliable estimates from a smaller group when tracking down every single person is too difficult. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h2)

question: What does a demographic rate typically measure?

options.A: The weight of medical equipment in a ward
options.B: The physical size of a community health center
options.C: The exact total money spent on healthcare
options.D: How often an event happens in a population over time

explanation: Rates show the frequency of specific occurrences, like births or deaths, relative to the total population size over a given period. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h3)

question: A public health nurse wants to measure how many live births occurred per one thousand people in a town over one year. Which rate should be calculated?
explanation: The Crude Birth Rate specifically calculates live births per one thousand population in a defined one-year period. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h3)

question: What does morbidity measure in a community?

options.A: The state of being unhealthy or diseased
options.B: The total number of registered deaths
options.C: The number of new babies born in a year
options.D: The amount of money earned by hospitals

explanation: Morbidity focuses on illness, sickness, and disease prevalence rather than death itself. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses to study both morbidity and mortality statistics together?

options.A: To prove that nobody gets sick in rural areas
options.B: To replace the need for physical patient examinations
options.C: To see which illnesses cause suffering versus which ones cause death
options.D: To calculate the exact salary of medical doctors

explanation: Looking at both illness rates and death rates provides a complete picture of the total health burden affecting a population. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: What does the Infant Mortality Rate measure?

options.A: Babies who die before reaching their first birthday
options.B: Children under five years old who get malaria
options.D: Total number of babies born in a hospital

explanation: Infant Mortality Rate specifically tracks deaths occurring during the first year of life per one thousand live births. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h5)

question: High rates of under-five mortality in a community usually point to problems with which of the following?

options.B: Lack of secondary school education for adults
options.C: High rates of retirement among elderly workers

explanation: Child deaths under five are largely driven by malnutrition, poor sanitation, and preventable childhood infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is a major reason why vital statistics are often incomplete in rural Nigeria?

options.A: Every citizen has a personal digital health computer
options.B: Hospitals refuse to admit pregnant women
options.C: Too many people work as professional statisticians
options.D: Many births and deaths happen at home and go unreported

explanation: Home deliveries and unreported home deaths mean many vital events never make it into official government records. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is a direct consequence of having weak vital data collection systems in a country?

options.A: Doctors will have less paperwork to complete daily
options.B: Citizens will stop falling sick from infectious diseases
options.C: Hospitals will automatically receive excess funding
options.D: Health planners rely on estimates that may lead to poor interventions

explanation: Inaccurate or missing data forces decision-makers to guess where resources are needed, resulting in poorly targeted health programs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h6)

question: How do health ministries primarily use vital statistics data?

options.A: To test the speed of computer networks in wards
options.B: To decide which medications taste best
options.C: To allocate medical budgets and place facilities
options.D: To grade nursing students on final exams

explanation: Governments use population data to figure out where to spend money and build clinics based on real community needs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h7)

question: A state health board notices a sharp rise in infant mortality in a rural district through vital data. What action should they take first?

options.A: Increase taxes for citizens living in urban areas
options.B: Close all the primary schools in the affected region
options.C: Stop collecting birth data for the next five years
options.D: Direct more child health resources and immunisation teams to that district

explanation: When data highlights a specific problem area, health planners must channel targeted interventions directly to that community to save lives. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h7)
